procedure.step: Register the factory with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism (if not already registered). The factory must be located outside a free zone, hold a MoIAT industrial licence, and provide a letter confirming 40% domestic value added; processing takes about three working days.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: Log in to the ministry e-services portal and select the Certificate of Origin for India service.
Complete the application form with the HS code, description, quantity and value of the product; each item must qualify separately.
Upload the required documents: proof of factory registration, the commercial invoice, and, if a trading exporter, the factory's purchase invoice.
Pay the certificate fee online. The fee for an invoice value up to AED 100,000 is AED 50.
Submit the application. Processing takes about one working day.
The certificate must be issued before, at, or within five working days of export; it is valid for twelve months from issue and covers one import.
Ship the goods directly from the UAE to India; transit through another country is allowed only under customs control with no operations other than unloading, reloading or storage.
Provide the certificate to the Indian importer, who will claim the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and must hold origin information under CAROTAR 2020.
Keep origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least five years from the end of the calendar year of the certificate's issue.

caveats.note: The duty estimate is based on the shipment value given (100,000 AED). India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; no conversion is done.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, the Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
The '+' in the product-specific rule is interpreted as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
The origin checks (final manufacture and minimal operations) are based on the exporter's own declaration.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' (used in the build-up method) are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not state whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
A product that only undergoes the minimal operations listed in Article 3.5.1 (e.g., simple assembly, packaging, labelling) does not originate, even if it meets its product-specific rule.
Interpretation: de minimis helps only the tariff-shift part of a rule, not the VA percentage.

Cumulation is bilateral only: originating materials from India used in production in the UAE may be counted as originating, but the last production process in the UAE must still go beyond the minimal operations.

For a retrospectively issued certificate, the agreement says box 8 for the 'ISSUED RETROSPECTIVELY' mark, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum for record keeping; the CEPA's 5-year requirement governs CEPA claims.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, which is required before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
The Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) is likely charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text on it was found).
Anti-dumping and safeguard duties likely still apply (no CEPA exemption from them was found).
Electronic certificates from the UAE issuing authority are accepted and uploaded to e-Sanchit by the importer or customs broker.
